questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of the 'Repository' pattern in Domain-Driven Design?
questions.explanation: A Repository mediates between the domain and data mapping layers using a collection-like interface for accessing domain objects.

options.text: To provide a collection-like interface for accessing domain objects.
To validate user input in the UI.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are advantages of using a 'Layered Architecture'?
questions.explanation: Layered architectures support separation of concerns (e.g., UI vs. Logic) and testability (layers can be tested in isolation). They do *not* necessarily improve performance due to overhead.

options.text: Separation of concerns (e.g., UI separate from Business Logic).

questions.question_text: Classify the following as 'Whitebox' or 'Blackbox' views of a component.
questions.explanation: Whitebox reveals internal details (sub-components, logic). Blackbox hides details and shows only interfaces/responsibilities.

rows.text: A diagram showing internal classes and their relationships.
A description of the public interface and service guarantees.
A sequence diagram of internal method calls.
A specification of input/output data formats only.

questions.question_text: What does the 'I' in SOLID stand for?
questions.explanation: I stands for Interface Segregation Principle: Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical 'Quality Attributes' defined in ISO 25010?
questions.explanation: Reliability, Usability, and Security are top-level quality characteristics in ISO 25010. 'Cost' and 'Timeline' are project constraints, not software quality attributes.

questions.question_text: Assign the following concerns to the correct view: 'Deployment View' or 'Runtime View'.
questions.explanation: Deployment View deals with hardware mapping and network topology. Runtime View deals with object interaction, data flow, and timing.

rows.text: Mapping of software artifacts to servers.
Sequence of messages during a login process.
Network bandwidth requirements between nodes.

questions.question_text: Which pattern provides a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem?
questions.explanation: The Facade pattern defines a higher-level interface that makes the subsystem easier to use by wrapping a complex set of interfaces.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following statements about 'Coupling' are true?
questions.explanation: Low coupling is desirable because it reduces the impact of changes. Tight coupling means components are highly dependent on each other, making maintenance harder.

options.text: Tight coupling makes systems easier to maintain.
Coupling measures the degree of interdependence between modules.
Coupling and Cohesion are the same thing.

questions.question_text: Determine if the following are 'Functional Requirements' or 'Constraints'.
questions.explanation: Constraints restrict design choices (technology, legal). Functional requirements specify system behavior.

rows.text: The system must use an Oracle database due to company policy.
The system must calculate VAT for invoices.
The application must be written in C#.
Users must be able to search for products by name.

questions.question_text: What is the main goal of the 'Model-View-Controller' (MVC) pattern?
questions.explanation: MVC separates the user interface (View) from the business logic (Model) and the user input handling (Controller) to improve maintainability and testability.

options.text: To combine all logic into one class.
To separate internal representation of information from the way it is presented to the user.
To encrypt data in the database.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are essential parts of the 'arc42' documentation template?
questions.explanation: Introduction/Goals, Building Block View, and Runtime View are core arc42 sections. 'Marketing Plan' and 'Employee Salary List' are not.

questions.question_text: Decide if the following concepts relate to 'High Cohesion' or 'Low Cohesion'.
questions.explanation: High cohesion means a module does one thing well (focused). Low cohesion means a module does many unrelated things (random features).

rows.text: A class has a single, well-defined responsibility.
A 'Utility' class contains random, unrelated helper methods.
A module groups functions that operate on the same data entity.

questions.question_text: What is the primary benefit of 'Architecture Decision Records' (ADRs)?
questions.explanation: ADRs capture the context and rationale (the 'why') of important decisions, preventing knowledge loss and helping future maintainers understand the history.

options.text: They document the rationale and context of architectural decisions for future reference.
They replace the need for requirements engineering.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are characteristics of 'Event-Driven Architecture'?
questions.explanation: Event-driven systems are decoupled (producers don't know consumers) and asynchronous (processing happens when events arrive). They are typically not synchronous or monolithic.

options.text: Decoupling of event producers and consumers.

questions.question_text: Match the UML diagram to its category: 'Structure' or 'Behavior'.
questions.explanation: Class diagrams show static structure. Activity, Sequence, and State Machine diagrams show dynamic behavior.

rows.text: Class Diagram
Activity Diagram
Sequence Diagram
State Machine Diagram

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the 'Context View'?
questions.explanation: The Context View defines the system boundary, identifying external interfaces and neighboring systems (actors). It treats the system as a black box.

options.text: To show the internal class hierarchy.
To delimit the system from its environment and identify external interfaces.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical responsibilities of a Software Architect?
questions.explanation: Architects design structure, evaluate technical risks, and communicate with stakeholders. Writing all the code or selling the product are usually not their primary responsibilities.

options.text: Writing every line of code personally.

questions.question_text: Decide if the statement relates to 'Microservices' or 'Monolith'.
questions.explanation: Monoliths are single deployment units. Microservices are distributed, independently deployable units.

rows.text: Single deployment unit containing all functionality.
Distributed system with independently deployable services.
Tends to be easier to debug initially (single process).

questions.question_text: What is 'Technical Debt'?
questions.explanation: Technical Debt refers to the implied cost of future reworking required when choosing an easy/quick solution now instead of a better approach that would take longer.

options.text: The implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now.
The monthly fee for cloud hosting.

questions.question_text: Assign the following attributes to the correct ISO 25010 category: 'Reliability' or 'Portability'.
questions.explanation: Reliability includes Availability and Fault Tolerance. Portability includes Adaptability and Installability.

rows.text: Availability
Adaptability
Fault Tolerance
Installability

questions.question_text: What is the core concept of the 'Broker' architectural pattern?
questions.explanation: The Broker pattern structures distributed systems with decoupled components that interact by remote service invocations. A broker component is responsible for coordinating communication, such as forwarding requests, as well as for transmitting results and exceptions.

options.text: All components share a central memory space (blackboard).
A central component coordinates communication between decoupled client and server objects.
Data flows through a sequence of processing steps.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are valid methods for 'Architecture Evaluation'?
questions.explanation: ATAM (Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method), Prototypes/PoCs, and Reviews are standard evaluation methods. 'User Interface Testing' focuses on usability/functionality, not necessarily architectural structure.

questions.question_text: Classify the following as 'Top-Down' or 'Bottom-Up' approaches.
questions.explanation: Top-Down starts with the big picture/requirements and decomposes. Bottom-Up starts with existing details/code and abstracts upwards.

rows.text: Deriving the system context from the business requirements.
Analyzing existing database tables to understand the data model.
Grouping existing classes into packages/modules.

questions.question_text: What does the 'Dependency Inversion Principle' typically require?
questions.explanation: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions (e.g., interfaces).

options.text: High-level modules should depend on low-level modules.
High-level modules and low-level modules should depend on abstractions.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following statements about 'Cross-Cutting Concepts' are true?
questions.explanation: Concepts ensure consistency across the system and prevent redundancy by defining a standard way to solve recurring problems (like logging or security).

options.text: They are relevant for multiple parts of the system.
They always map 1:1 to a single class.
They are only relevant for the user interface.

questions.question_text: Assign the following elements to 'Business Context' or 'Technical Context'.
questions.explanation: Business Context deals with domain actors and logical data exchange. Technical Context deals with transport protocols, hardware, and file formats.

rows.text: Customer (Human Actor)
HTTPS / TLS 1.3
Administrator (Role)
JSON over TCP/IP

questions.question_text: Which pattern separates the abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independently?
questions.explanation: The Bridge pattern decouples an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independently.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are benefits of the 'Microservices' architectural style?
questions.explanation: Microservices allow for independent deployment (agility) and independent scalability of services. They often *increase* operational complexity compared to a monolith.

options.text: Guaranteed ACID transactions across the whole system.

questions.question_text: Decide if the statement describes 'Architecture' or 'Implementation Details'.
questions.explanation: Architecture concerns high-level structure, major decisions, and public interfaces. Implementation details concern local variable names, specific algorithms within a method, and private helper classes.

rows.text: The naming convention for private variables inside a method.
The decision to use a layered style with strict layering.
The definition of the public interfaces between subsystems.

questions.question_text: What is 'Conway's Law'?
questions.explanation: Organizations which design systems are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations.

options.text: The number of transistors on a chip doubles every two years.
Organizations design systems that mirror their own communication structure.
Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical 'Constraints' that influence software architecture?
questions.explanation: Budget, Time/Deadline, and Regulatory Compliance are external constraints. 'Personal preference' should ideally not be a primary driver compared to business/technical needs.

options.text: Available Skill Set of the Team

questions.question_text: Match the description to the correct diagram type.
questions.explanation: Sequence diagrams show time-ordered interactions. Deployment diagrams show physical nodes. Activity diagrams show control flow.

rows.text: Shows interaction between objects ordered by time.
Shows mapping of artifacts to hardware nodes.
Shows the flow of control and data between steps.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the 'Solution Strategy' section in arc42?
questions.explanation: Section 4 'Solution Strategy' gives a condensed summary of the fundamental decisions and solution ideas to solve the core problems/goals.

options.text: To summarize the fundamental decisions and approaches to meet the goals.
To show the full source code.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following patterns are primarily used for 'Resilience' (Fault Tolerance)?
questions.explanation: Circuit Breaker and Bulkhead are resilience patterns. Circuit Breaker prevents cascading failures. Bulkhead isolates failures to a specific pool. MVC and Factory are design/structural patterns.

questions.question_text: Decide if the statement is True or False regarding 'Documentation'.
questions.explanation: Documentation should be target-group oriented (different views for different stakeholders). It should not be 'write-only' (useless if no one reads it).

rows.text: Documentation should be tailored to the needs of specific stakeholders.
The best documentation is the one that covers every single line of code.
Architecture documentation complements the source code.

questions.question_text: What is the goal of the 'Adapter' pattern?
questions.explanation: The Adapter pattern converts the interface of a class into another interface clients expect. It lets classes work together that couldn't otherwise because of incompatible interfaces.

options.text: To create only one instance of a class.
To convert the interface of a class into another interface the client expects.
To define a family of algorithms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are examples of 'Internal Interfaces' (Building Block View)?
questions.explanation: Java interfaces and REST APIs between internal microservices are internal interfaces. The GUI for the end-user is a system boundary/external interface. A power cable is physical, not logical software architecture.

options.text: A Java interface definition used between two packages.
The User Interface (GUI) for the end-user.
A REST API call between two internal microservices.
The power cable of the server.

questions.question_text: Which principle states: 'Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification'?
questions.explanation: This is the exact definition of the Open-Closed Principle (OCP).
